purpose: Verify how installed MDVx reads, stores and uses PMR FileMobId/MasterMobId, separately from proposed Bella behavior.
method: Existing Hopper pseudo-C re-read and cross-checked with bounded native instructions, Objective-C methods and actual Mach-O comparator-block bindings. No runtime scan.

readingAndStorage.scope: Read-only arm64 static instruction/Objective-C metadata verification against earlier Hopper exports. No MDVx scan/private API execution or repository/media changes.

parser.retainedRecord: Makes NSMutableData copy of complete passed PMR record slice at0x1000304b0; stores retained buffer at item+0x70.
parser.widthFlag: Internal DB_SizeofUID is2 forv2 and8 forv8/v16 (32-bit word count, not byte count).

identityStorage.metadata: Objective-C MDVxUUID union has UMIDx[32C]; filePackageUID atitem+0x8, materialPackageUID atitem+0x28; each32bytes.
identityStorage.legacyWrapper: The inspected init/parser do not construct Avid prefix/suffix around the legacy core; init sets pointer fields to the two preallocated32byte slots.
identityStorage.byteOrder: Copies ID bytes unchanged in this PMR routine. usebyteswap swaps16bit filename/project length words at0x100030558..568 and0x1000305e8..5f8; no ID field swapping occurs here. checkUUID only checks/logs prefix for modernIDs.

formatting.modern: Formats all32bytes ashex at0x100031128..17c, inserting hyphens every4bytes.
formatting.storedVsDisplay: Item storage is binary; getFileUIDString/getMaterialUIDString request readable string formatting.

comparisons.isEqualByUUID: 0x1000302e0: hashcheck then compare two32bitwords atFileIDoffset16/20 (0x100030338..364). Doesnotcomparefull32byteFileID orMasterID.
comparisons.isEqual: 0x1000301b0: callsisEqualByUUID thenrequires nonnull identicalDB_itemPath.path at0x100030288. Thus inspectedordinaryitemequality includespath, notonlythe8bytekey.

mdbLookup.master: DB_materialPackageUID+0x10 at0x100064804..4810 feedsUIDtoBentoObj initWithUID, then mastertree lookup0x100064820.
mdbLookup.matchingScope: Both MDB lookups use8bytes atoffset16 ofID; they do not comparefull32bytes.

qualifications: Fullmodern IDs are retained and displayed; describingMDVxasstoringonly8byteswouldbeincorrect. Itslookup/equalitykeysare8bytes.
No realcollision between distinct32byteIDs wasdemonstrated. Theinspectedcomparisoncannot distinguishIDsdifferingonlyoutsideits8bytecore.
No independent endian-format runtime test or workload benchmark wasexecuted.

useAndComparisons.scope: Read-only installed MDVx 0.2 build4073 arm64 ID use; native instructions cross-checked with existing Hopper pseudo-C; no runtime scan.
conclusions: MDVx uses the ID roles similarly to the proposed Bella flow: file identity locates file metadata; material/master identity locates master-owned name/classification metadata.
The inspected MDB and ordinary AVB matching uses only an eight-byte excerpt at offset16 of the 32-byte IDs, not full32byte comparisons.
Ordinary item duplicate equality requires equal eight-byte file-ID excerpt and equal file path; different-path copies are not equal under this comparator.
Ordinary AVB filtering extracts eight-byte identities by scanning bytes for fixed markers; this method does not traverse the actual bin source/track graph.
Bin filtering compares file identity excerpt and iterates all equal-key inventory entries, so matching copies at different paths can all pass.
No measured speed benefit or exhaustive correctness/coverage is established.

MDBLookup.enabledBy: MDVxPMRScannerOperation reads ScanMDB preference and opens sibling msmMMOB.mdb or fallback amaMMOB.mdb; calls addInfoToItem for PMRrows

equality.fullItem: isEqual0x1000301b0 first callsisEqualByUUID then compares DB_itemPath.path strings at0x100030288
equality.sort: isLessByUUID0x100030390 sorts same two32bitfileUIDwords; database_LT block adds paths as tie-breaker

makeUnique.limit: Exact retained winner among equivalent duplicate entries not established here.

ordinaryAVB.copy: 0x100036960..0x100036970 copies eightbytes after marker into DatabaseItem fileUID+0x10
ordinaryAVB.handoff: AVBArray_IntersectWith0x10004b138 collects getUIDS arrays and callsapplyFilter at0x10004b27c
ordinaryAVB.applyFilter: 0x10004c5d8 builds a tree of inventoryitems using ID-only equality/ordering
ordinaryAVB.search: 0x10004c7a0 searches for bin-extracted ID;0x10004c800 TreefindNextEQ iterates allmatchingentries
ordinaryAVB.limit: AMA bin paths exist separately; this describes ordinary getUIDS path, not exhaustive AVB workflows.

limits: Static inspected paths only; no new decompilation, timed scan, workload benchmark or live MDVx action.
ID parsing/byte normalization is assigned to another agent; this receipt focuses use/comparisons.
Eight-byte key equality can equate fullIDs differing outside that excerpt; no claim that such collision occurred in user media.
No conclusion that MasterID is never used elsewhere; here it supplies master metadata but not ordinary AVB membership comparator.

genuineSampleKeyCheck.scope: Eight-byte lookup-excerpt comparison in previously inspected version-16 records, with file and master namespaces kept separate. This is not a proof for arbitrary Avid IDs.

comparisonWithBellaProposal.similarity: Binary ID reading; folder+filename physical association; FileMobId for file metadata and MasterMobId for associated-master metadata.
comparisonWithBellaProposal.difference: The inspected MDVx MDB and ordinary bin matching compare only the eight-byte ID excerpt; Bella retains complete identities for the approved scanner/parser work. The existing Bin Filter system remains unchanged and outside Bella.
comparisonWithBellaProposal.status: The user approved complete ID reading and the path-plus-FileMobId duplicate rule for the scanner/parser. Internal storage details remain open; no Bin Filter changes are required.

limits: No timed scan or performance advantage measured.
No claim that excerpt collisions occurred in the inspected media; none found in the file-ID or master-ID sample namespace.
Different full IDs outside the compared excerpt cannot be distinguished by the inspected short-key comparators.
Exact winner among equivalent duplicate items remains unestablished.
Ordinary AVB marker scanning and ID filtering were traced; separate AMA paths are not exhaustively covered.
The byte-swap observation is scoped to the PMR item parser, not every MDVx identity-reading path.

approvedBellaIdentityRules.fullIds: Read complete FileMobId and MasterMobId, not only an eight-byte excerpt of modern IDs. Respect complete legacy representations when falling back.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.kelpieId: Retain current internal MediaMuster scan-session row identifier, independent of Avid IDs.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.samePathAndSameFileMobId: Ignore duplicate inventory entry; keep existing row and KelpieId.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.differentPathAndSameFileMobId: Keep each row with its own unique KelpieId.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.scope: Inventory row duplication; eligible metadata may still enrich the kept row. No new cross-scan persistence specified.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.samePathConflictingFileMobIds: For release one, the user explicitly assumes this cannot happen. Do not add conflict-handling machinery.

binFilterScopeClarification.status: User scope clarification; existing Bin Filter system remains unchanged
binFilterScopeClarification.userInstruction: This scope is for the Scanner/parser system. We are leaving the Bin Filter system alone, just confirmed that MDVX also uses FileMobId to filter Bins.
binFilterScopeClarification.scope: Bella replaces the scanner/parser system only. The Bin Filter system is outside Bella and remains unchanged; no new bin algorithm, matching or per-row behavior is required.
binFilterScopeClarification.comparisonConfirmed: The inspected MDVx bin filtering uses FileMobId identity; that comparison does not approve changes to MediaMuster Bin Filter behavior.

approvedBellaSetFallback.userInstruction: For now, the first release of the app: lets keep it basic and straight forward. If an entry is damaged, abandon the set and fall back to another set. How should we determine this?
approvedBellaSetFallback.damagedRecord: Any damaged record makes its entire set unusable; do not salvage individual records or combine metadata from the two sets.
approvedBellaSetFallback.setSelection: Prefer a usable version-16 set. If it is missing or unusable, use the older set only if that whole set is usable.
approvedBellaSetFallback.neitherUsable: Use no PMR metadata when neither set is usable. Keep the physical media-file inventory independently.
approvedBellaSetFallback.validationStatus: User-approved release-one damage and usability checks on 18 October 2026; not implemented.
approvedBellaSetFallback.validationApproval: OK, let's lock those checks in for Bella.

approvedChecks.completeEntry: Every declared record must contain all bytes required by its supported version: complete IDs, length words and counted text payloads, and the four bounded skipped modification bytes. A short record makes its whole set unusable.
approvedChecks.lengthsAndCounts: Stored text lengths and record counts must fit the available data; an overrun or impossible count makes the whole set unusable.
approvedChecks.version16Filename: Require the verified v16 filename framing and strict UTF-8. Its two reserved prefix bytes must be present and the first zero; the native PMR helper does not constrain the second. Invalid framing or UTF-8 makes the whole set unusable.
approvedChecks.emptyFilename: An empty or null Filename makes the whole set unusable because it cannot associate that entry with a physical file. This is a Bella usability rule, not proof of structural corruption.
approvedChecks.emptySet: A set with no entries supplies no usable PMR metadata; fall back to the other usable set.

notDamage: Fields legitimately absent in older versions, including v1 Project and MasterMobId
Different entry counts between the older and version-16 sets
A database reference to a physical file that has since disappeared
approvedBellaSetFallback.safeVersion16Location: The older set physically precedes v16. Follow its lengths and counts safely to locate v16; if damaged framing makes that boundary unknowable, ignore PMR metadata rather than search for a plausible version word. Keep physical inventory.
approvedBellaSetFallback.validationLimit: These checks cannot detect every incorrect value with a valid representation. MacRoman accepts every byte, so successful decoding does not prove a Project character is correct. Ignored modification values are not inspected for semantic validity.
